proof_skeleton_nl: Start with a numerical semigroup S. By standard semigroup facts, the conductor c exists, the set L = S ∩ [0,c-1] is finite, and the minimal generating set exists and has finite cardinality e. Next count the integers in [0,c-1]: those in S contribute |L| and those outside S contribute g, so c = |L| + g. Rearranging shows that the desired inequality e|L| >= c is equivalent to (e-1)|L| >= g. At this point the argument reaches the classical Wilf conjecture in genus form. Since no general proof of that final inequality is known, the decomposition cannot honestly be completed into a proof of the universal root theorem using only true established lemmas.

steps.derives: For any numerical semigroup S, the quantities e = |MinGen(S)|, c = conductor(S), and L = {s in S : s < c} are all well-defined, with e a positive integer and L finite.
steps.trivial_justification: L1 gives existence of the conductor c. L2 gives that L = S ∩ [0,c-1] is finite. L3 gives existence and finiteness of the minimal generating set and hence of e = |MinGen(S)|.

steps.derives: If g denotes the number of gaps below the conductor, then c = |L| + g.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the statement of L5 after the objects are known to be well-defined from A1.

steps.derives: The target inequality e * |L| >= c is equivalent to the inequality (e - 1) * |L| >= g.
The root theorem would follow if one had a further valid lemma asserting (e - 1) * |L| >= g for every numerical semigroup S.
steps.trivial_justification: A3 reduces the theorem to the genus inequality. However, no universally valid proved lemma establishing this bound is currently known in full generality; that missing statement is exactly an equivalent form of the open Wilf conjecture.
